subject: convoyHauler
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: armoured convoy hauler guarding a sealed cargo pod.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk.
reasoning:
I'm planning a moderately detailed static vehicle model—a heavy armoured truck with a cab, armour plates, cargo pod, neon glow strips, decal textures like warning stripes and lights, plus a roof turret, keeping it simple without joints since wheels can just be static parts.

Working out dimensions and layout: roughly 9m long, 2.8m wide, 3.4m tall, with six wheels (radius ~0.55-0.62) arranged as a front axle and rear tandem, a cargo pod toward the back, and a wedge-shaped cab up front with a sloped windshield for the cyberpunk look. I'm planning helper functions for boxes and wheels (tires, tread blocks, rims, hubs, lug nuts) while keeping part counts reasonable.

Defining the cab's extruded cross-section profile...

For the windshield, I'm computing the slanted plane's normal and dimensions from the slope geometry, offsetting it slightly outward with a cyan HUD-style texture. Then I'm positioning side window planes on the cab's flanks, working out their x/z/y bounds from the uv region mapped to world coordinates.

Now I'm placing the headlights: a glowing light bar centered on the sloped front face, plus quad headlight shapes and a grille texture, all positioned relative to the hood's front u/v coordinates to line up with the bumper box below.

I'm working out the plow/bumper geometry — using a hazard-striped plane for the bumper face instead of stretching a box texture, then designing a cow-catcher wedge via an extruded side profile with angled points to form the triangular blade shape.

Now I'm moving on to the chassis frame: two long beams running front-to-back, plus considering fuel tank cylinders and side skirts between the wheels.

For wheel fenders, I'm building arch-shaped covers over each wheel using a low-poly semicircle outline extruded sideways, positioning them at the wheel centers with width matching the tire. I'm placing the wheels at x = ±1.45 with radius 0.62, keeping them outside the wider cab body.

Checking clearances: the cab needs to sit at roughly 2.3 wide (±1.15) so it doesn't collide with the wheel arches, and the front wheels tuck under the hood near z=3.0. Now I'm starting to shape the cargo pod sitting on the flatbed, considering a swept polygon or hexagonal cross-section to build a capsule-like container.

Setting up the lathe parameters for the pod...

I'll make the bands use the same lathe geometry, segments, and spin as the pod so they align properly instead of using mismatched cylinder segments, with ring outlines at radius 1.2 and 1.36. For details, I'm adding a "SEALED" plate decal and glowing neon seam strips along the pod's top.

For the neon rods, rather than guessing facet orientations, I'll use surface hits on the pod to seat decals correctly at specific azimuth/elevation angles, placing hazard decals on the sides using hit normals for direction. Then I'm adding an end cap near the cab-facing side with a hatch plate and locking bolts where the dome geometry ends.

I'll put a rear hatch disc at the back of the pod using a surface hit facing backward, with a circular airlock texture and chevron decals, plus lock-clamp arm boxes connecting bed to pod. For the truck's rear, I'm adding a glowing red taillight strip, bumper, and mudflaps, then building a roof turret on the cab with a ring base, box body, twin barrel rods, and a glowing sight, positioned toward the rear of the roof and oriented to face forward. Finally I'm adding a roof light bar with orange/pink glow and antenna rods.

Now I'm working out exhaust stack placement — two vertical pipes behind the cab with heat shield bands and caps — checking clearance against the cab rear, pod front dome, and wheel positions so nothing overlaps, and settling on mounting them slightly wider at x ±1.25 starting from the fender line.

I'm adding bolted armor panels to the cab sides, plus door details: panel lines via texture decal, a door region with window placement, and a sign plate below the window reading "CV-07 / AEGIS" — making sure the mirrored text reads correctly when viewed from the opposite side.

I'm listing out the texture set needed: windshield, side windows, hazard stripes, door sign, pod logo, hatch, grille, and a few more, then deciding glow strength per part — modest glow for windows, strong for headlights, plus magenta underglow rods beneath the chassis. I'm keeping the overall code budget around 400 lines and starting to define the color palette.

Working out materials and wheel helper...

Still designing wheel geometry...

Still defining fender geometry...

Checking bed width against fender overlap and pod radius clearance at wheel arch height, adjusting dimensions so they fit without collision. Moving on to chassis beams and axle specs.

Working out axle positions relative to wheel clearances, placing differential housing and cross members, then checking if side battery pack boxes fit in the gap between front and rear wheels without interfering with ground clearance — adding glow strips and bolt details to them. Starting to place the rear bumper position.

Now I'm adding a rear bumper box with glowing red taillights, an underride bar, hitch, and mudflaps behind the wheels, then working through options for how to cradle the pod against the chassis — trying extruded arch ribs versus simple angled wedge boxes before settling on a saddle-shaped cradle outline to hold the pod.

Writing cradle outline coordinates...

I'm sketching the turret body with twin barrels and muzzle brakes, positioning it on the roof so it clears the pod and windshield heights without clipping anything.

Now I'm adding the light bar across the roof's front edge with glowing cyan/magenta halves, a sweeping antenna rod with a glowing tip reaching up to about 4.4 height, and starting to work out mirror arms and inset vent slats along the sloped hood profile.

Placing three hood slats with decreasing v values as they move forward, tilted along the hood slope and lifted slightly off the surface. Now I'm positioning the front grille plane near the vertical face of the hood front, figuring out its y and z coordinates to align with the slope transition.

Figuring out the tilt for the front face plane since it leans forward as it rises, so the normal needs to point downward-forward rather than straight back. I'm placing the headlights as small glowing planes on either side and starting on a light bar positioned above them.

Now I'm working through the bumper geometry — placing a box below the body and shaping a wedge-like ram plate at the front using a triangular cross-section, trying to get the slope facing the right direction so the lower edge sticks out further than the top.

Rather than a smooth ramp, I decide to go with a chamfered bumper fitted with angled cone-shaped spikes across the front for a brutalist, cyberpunk look — five teeth spaced along the width. I'm also sketching a hazard-stripe texture (amber background with black diagonal parallelograms) to apply as a decal on the bumper's front face.

For the windows I'm designing a dark teal gradient windshield texture with HUD lines and pink reflection streaks, and for the cargo pod I'm creating a "sealed cargo" emblem — a hexagon with chevron details — positioned as side decals on the pod's flanks using explicit surface coordinates.

Now I'm adding neon strips along the top of the pod as raised rods, calculating their placement by raycasting down from above to find the hit height, and constraining the z-range to where the pod's flat top section actually exists.

Now I'm adding pod roof details like a rotating amber beacon light and sensor puck, plus thinking through armour panel plates on the cab sides near the doors, sized to fit the door and window regions with bolted detailing.

Placing door armour plates with signage and corner bolt cylinders...

I'm also adding a sensor backplate with a glowing slit near the cab rear, plus guard cage ribs, and double-checking that the wheel tread blocks sit flush with the ground without clipping below the floor.

With dimensions settled, I'm defining helper functions for boxes and cylinders to streamline building each part, and sorting out color conventions for painted hull parts versus flat-colored glowing components.

For the hull I'm designing a custom grime paint function that mixes a base metallic tone with noise variation, adds dirt streaks toward the bottom, and a lighter highlight near the top edges, then layering that into a panelled material with rivets for the armor plating look.

For the pods I'm sketching a lighter mottled colorway—blending soft blue-grays with some countershading—then wrapping that into the same panelled rivet treatment but with slightly different size and aspect ratios to differentiate them from the hull.

Now I'm moving onto the texture SVGs: a hazard stripe pattern with amber and dark chevrons, and a door placard with a dark plate, cyan outline, and bold amber "CV-07" text alongside smaller escort labeling.

Writing SVG code...

I place underglow rods outside the chassis beams to avoid overlap, skip the window porthole idea, and set up mirrored side parts using sign flips for x position and direction. Now starting the actual build script with imports from the builder library.

Importing clockwork and glow kits...

I'm setting up the lathe profile for the pod shape using an octagonal outline, with ring bands positioned at relative z offsets along the pod's length.

Calculating band positions and taper radii...

I'm also planning decal placements for the rear pod hatch at the tip of the dome, and considering a sensor pad or pressure valve detail for the front end of the pod.

For the valve assembly I'm using a steel cylinder with a wheel attached, then a roof beacon placed via a raycast hit at the top of the pod dome, along with vent boxes positioned symmetrically. I'm also weighing whether to add a rear ladder with rails and rungs near the back of the pod, though I may skip it to keep things simpler.

I decide to drop the ladder and handrails entirely, focusing instead on mudflaps behind the rear tandem wheels sized around .6x.5x.04 and hanging just below the chassis, using the spike helper function with a base point, direction, length, radius, and a slate-gray color for small greebles.

Now I'm extruding the cab shape with the hull paint color, setting its position and thickness with a slight bevel, then adding hood side plates before finalizing the write.
